verdict_reason: The tests use the shared row fixtures and test through inputs and outputs, but the resultRows title claims more than its single-species input proves.

todos.issue: The title 'Should give one row per species in the search results, with its code' claims a row per species, but the input has one group with one species, so an implementation that returned one row per group (or only the first species) would still pass.
todos.fix: Must: the test's input has at least one group with more than one species (and ideally two groups), and the assertion proves every species becomes its own row carrying its group's code. One way: use a 0102 group with BOS_TAURUS_ROW and BISON_BISON_ROW plus the 01061900 group with FELIS_CATUS_ROW, and expect all three rows in order.
